headline: Fakhar Zaman's 127 powers Pakistan to tri-series title over Sri Lanka
summary: Pakistan chased down 326 to win the ODI tri-series final in Lahore, securing their first title since 2008.
details: Fakhar Zaman's superb 127 off 99 balls anchored Pakistan's three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the One-Day International tri-series final in Lahore on Saturday.
Chasing a target of 326, Pakistan finished on 331 with nine balls to spare, completing one of the joint-highest successful chases in an ODI final.
Sri Lanka had posted a formidable 325 for eight, driven by Kamindu Mendis' maiden ODI century (131 off 128 balls) and Pavan Rathnayake's 77.
Pakistan faced early trouble when Dilshan Madushanka took two early wickets, including Babar Azam for a duck, but Zaman and Saad Baig rebuilt with a 149-run stand.

This victory marks Pakistan's first ODI tri-series title since 2008, when they defeated India in the Kitply Cup final in Bangladesh.
caption:
A massive chase and a century for the ages! Pakistan secures its first ODI tri-series title since 2008.

Fakhar Zaman's superb 127 off 99 balls anchored Pakistan's three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the One-Day International tri-series final in Lahore on Saturday.

Chasing a target of 326, Pakistan finished on 331 with nine balls to spare, completing one of the joint-highest successful chases in an ODI final.

Sri Lanka had posted a formidable 325 for eight, driven by Kamindu Mendis' maiden ODI century (131 off 128 balls) and Pavan Rathnayake's 77.

Pakistan faced early trouble when Dilshan Madushanka took two early wickets, including Babar Azam for a duck, but Zaman and Saad Baig rebuilt with a 149-run stand.

After Zaman fell, Arafat Minhas' half-century and a 94-run partnership with Hasan Nawaz ensured the hosts reached the target.

This victory marks Pakistan's first ODI tri-series title since 2008, when they defeated India in the Kitply Cup final in Bangladesh.

headline_marked: DB's Harun and 7 other [[police officers dismissed from service]]
headline: DB's Harun and 7 other police officers dismissed from service
summary: Seven police officers, including former DB inspector Harun, have been fired, while one other officer has been retired.
details: Seven police officers, including former Detective Branch (DB) officer Harun, have been dismissed from their jobs.
The decision comes as part of a broader cleanup of the police force following recent national developments.
In addition to the seven dismissed officers, one other police official has been placed on compulsory retirement.
The dismissals target high-ranking officials who were allegedly involved in misconduct or abuses of power during their tenure.
The action is seen as a move by the authorities to ensure accountability within the security forces.
